title: Being flat descends along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02L2)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For $i\in I$ let $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ be the base change of $f$ along $g_i$, the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f_i$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] for every $i\in I$, then $f$ is flat.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L2 (lemma-descending-property-flat, line 5833, with its proof: Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-flatness-descends for R -> R' faithfully flat), the direction 'each base change $X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ has the property $\Rightarrow$ $f$ has it' of 'fpqc local on the base', Descent, Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310)

proof.text: *Flatness is invariant under isomorphism and Zariski local on the base (conditions (0) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion] for $\mathcal P$ = flat).* By [def-weil-flat-morphism], $f:X\to S$ is flat at $x$ iff the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat. Isomorphisms $a:X\to\tilde X$, $b:S\to\tilde S$ with $\tilde fa=bf$ identify $\mathcal O_{\tilde S,\tilde f(a(x))}\to\mathcal O_{\tilde X,a(x)}$ with $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ through ring isomorphisms, so flatness is invariant under isomorphism. The local rings of an open subscheme are those of the ambient scheme [def-pc-scheme]; hence for an open $V\subseteq S$ and $x\in f^{-1}(V)$ the restriction $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is flat at $x$ iff $f$ is, and likewise for an open $U\subseteq X$ the morphism $f|_U:U\to S$ is flat at $x\in U$ iff $f$ is. So if $S=\bigcup_kV_k$ is an open covering and every $f^{-1}(V_k)\to V_k$ is flat, every $x\in X$ lies in some $f^{-1}(V_k)$ and $f$ is flat at $x$; and if $X=\bigcup U$ is an open covering with every $f|_U$ flat, $f$ is flat.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L2 (lemma-descending-property-flat, line 5833), proof: 'Being flat is Zariski local on the base by definition.'

proof.text: *Flatness is stable under base change (condition (1)).* If $f:X\to S$ is flat and $g:S'\to S$ is any morphism, in particular a flat one, the second projection $X\times_SS'\to S'$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L2 (lemma-descending-property-flat, line 5833), proof: 'Being flat is preserved under arbitrary base change, see Morphisms, Lemma 01U9 (morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat)'

proof.text: *Condition (3), the ring map of the base.* Let $g:S'\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes, $f:X\to S$ a morphism, $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to S'$, and assume $f'$ flat. By step 1 (invariance under isomorphism, applied to $f$, $g$ and $f'$) we may assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ [def-pc-scheme]; then $g=\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ for a unique ring map $\rho:R\to R'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $g$ is flat, $\rho$ is a flat ring map by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Since $g$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], the map of prime spectra $\mathfrak q\mapsto\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, which is the map of underlying sets of $\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], is surjective. Hence $\rho$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L2 (lemma-descending-property-flat, line 5833), proof: 'let S' -> S be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes ... We know that R -> R' is faithfully flat'

proof.text: *Condition (3), the base change of an affine open.* Keep the notation of step 3 and let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme]; then $f|_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha$ for a unique ring map $\alpha:R\to A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], making $A$ an $R$-algebra. Let $U'=g'^{-1}(U)$, an open subscheme of $X'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] (applied to $g'$ and $U$) the square formed by $U'\to U$, $U'\hookrightarrow X'$, $U\hookrightarrow X$, $g'$ is cartesian; it sits on top of the cartesian square $(X',g',f')$ of $f$ and $g$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the outer rectangle is cartesian: $U'$ with $U'\to U$ and $f'|_{U'}:U'\to S'$ is a fibre product $U\times_SS'$ of $f|_U$ and $g$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism, there is an isomorphism $U'\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RR')$ under which $f'|_{U'}$ becomes $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $R'\to A\otimes_RR'$, $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$. The morphism $f'|_{U'}$ is flat, as the restriction of the flat $f'$ to an open subscheme (step 1); by invariance under isomorphism (step 1) $\operatorname{Spec}(R'\to A\otimes_RR')$ is flat, so $R'\to A\otimes_RR'$ is a flat ring map by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Through the swap isomorphism $A\otimes_RR'\cong R'\otimes_RA$, $a\otimes r'\mapsto r'\otimes a$, which is $R'$-linear, this says: $R'\otimes_RA$ is a flat $R'$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L2 (lemma-descending-property-flat, line 5833), proof: 'Let U subset X be an affine open. Then U' = S' x_S U is affine. Write S = Spec(R), S' = Spec(R'), U = Spec(A), and U' = Spec(A'). We know that ... A' = R' otimes_R A and R' -> A' is flat.'

proof.text: *Condition (3), conclusion.* By step 3, $\rho:R\to R'$ is faithfully flat, and by step 4, $R'\otimes_RA$ is a flat $R'$-module; so $A$ is a flat $R$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flatness-descends-faithfully-flat] (with $M=A$), i.e. $\alpha$ is a flat ring map, and $f|_U=\operatorname{Spec}\alpha$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. The affine opens $U$ cover $X$ [def-pc-scheme], so $f$ is flat by step 1. Thus flatness satisfies condition (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02L2 (lemma-descending-property-flat, line 5833), proof: 'Goal: Show that R -> A is flat. This follows immediately from Algebra, Lemma 00HJ (algebra-lemma-flatness-descends). Hence f is flat.'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 1, 2 and 5 the class of flat morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism] satisfies conditions (0)-(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion]. Applied to $f:X\to S$ and the fpqc covering $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], whose base changes $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ are flat by hypothesis, it gives that $f$ is flat.
